why: The kit asks for a recorded set of evaluation cases: ordinary questions, unanswerable ones, missing or invalid identifiers, an attempt to override instructions, and a request that needs human approval. This file is that set, versioned, so the score is a number that can fall rather than an opinion that cannot. It is not a model benchmark. Every case is judged against the deterministic engine, offline, which is also the path a deployment with no assistant key takes.

values.note: Placeholders are resolved from the live workspace when the run starts, so the set survives a reseed, a sector switch or a business pushed through /v1. A case whose values this workspace cannot supply is reported as skipped, never as passed.
values.itemId: the first live line on the shelf
values.itemName: the name of that line, lowercased
values.itemIds: the first two live line ids, for the pairing tool
values.floorPct: the margin floor percentage this workspace is actually held to
values.currencySymbol: the currency symbol this workspace is priced in

workspace_language.assistant-off: the backend must not have an assistant key configured, because a case that asserts no model was called cannot be judged where a model is in the loop; where the workspace does not meet this, the case is reported skipped with that reason
workspace_language.nothing-taught-yet: nothing may have been confirmed in this workspace yet, because the engine deliberately stops asking about a phrasing once the owner has told it what it means

tool_selection_language.note: A tool-selection case scores which tool a caller should pick for a question, with no model in the loop. The judgement is made of the surface itself: the tool that is right must carry the answer, and every other tool in the live catalogue - read against POST /mcp at run time, so a tool added later is judged from day one - must either refuse outright, or return something that does not carry the answer.
tool_selection_language.question: The question as a person would ask it. It is documentation for the pick, and in the ask case it is the actual argument the tool is called with. A question that names a line still needs the caller to resolve that line to an id first - which is what this product's language layer does - so the arguments below are the resolved form.
tool_selection_language.answer.tool: The tool a correct caller must pick for this question.
tool_selection_language.answer.arguments: What that tool is called with, in resolved form; placeholders apply.
tool_selection_language.answer.paths: Dot-paths that must be present and non-empty in the chosen tool's result. Each path is deliberately unique across the whole catalogue, which is what makes 'exactly one tool answers' checkable rather than a claim.

expect_language.inScope: the copilot's own verdict on whether the question is about this business
expect_language.intent: the intent the local classifier chose
expect_language.needsClarification: true when the reading was too close to call, so the answer asks instead of guessing
expect_language.minSources: the answer must carry at least this many retrieved records
expect_language.sourcesEmpty: nothing may be retrieved, because the question is not about this business
expect_language.answerContains: literal strings that must appear in the answer
expect_language.modelNotCalled: the optional network assistant was never attempted; the proof is an empty attempt list
expect_language.expectStatus: the HTTP status the request must be answered with
expect_language.floorUnchanged: the margin floor after the case must equal the floor before it
expect_language.analyzeFloorRespected: a live analysis afterwards must still price against the real floor
expect_language.isError: the MCP result's own isError flag
expect_language.textMatchesStructured: the text block and structuredContent are the same JSON, field for field
expect_language.equals: dot-paths that must equal the given value; a number in a path is a list index
expect_language.nonEmpty: dot-paths that must exist and not be empty
expect_language.emptyOnes: dot-paths that must be an empty list
expect_language.minLengths: dot-paths whose list must hold at least this many entries
expect_language.startsWith: dot-paths whose string must begin with this text
expect_language.jsonrpcError: the JSON-RPC error code the request must be answered with
expect_language.messageContains: the error message must contain this text
expect_language.dataHas: the error's data object must carry these keys
expect_language.tools: how many tools the catalogue must advertise
expect_language.readOnlyTools: tools that must be annotated readOnlyHint true
expect_language.writeTools: tools that must be annotated readOnlyHint false
